questions.question: The prompt asked for rate limiting on the notes endpoint but did not specify whether it should apply per-IP or globally across all clients. If two different clients each send one request within the same 100 ms window, what does the implementation do — does each client get its own independent allowance, or does the second client get rate-limited because the first already consumed the single global slot?

No rate limit threshold was specified in the prompt. What effective maximum request rate (in requests per second) does the implementation enforce, and what would happen to a client that sends 15 requests spread evenly over one second — how many would succeed and how many would be rejected?

When the rate limit is exceeded, the implementation sends a specific HTTP response. Besides the 429 status code, what additional response header is included, and what value does it carry? If a client library automatically retries after honoring that header, how long would it wait before retrying?

questions.topic: Rate limiting applies to all methods equally
questions.question: The rate limiter sits before the method dispatch switch. Consider a scenario where a client sends a GET request immediately followed by a POST request within the same 100 ms window. What status code will the POST receive, and does the implementation treat read-only (GET) and write (POST) requests differently with respect to the rate limit?

The rate limiter uses a single 'next allowed time' variable rather than a sliding window or token bucket. If a client sends one request at time T and then waits exactly 100 ms before sending the next, will the second request succeed? What happens to the 'next allowed time' after the second request — does the window reset relative to T+100 ms or relative to when the second request actually arrives?
